text:
jules_support: Heads up — customer 'acme' opened a ticket: users are unable to complete MFA after a forced password reset. They report the web UI keeps redirecting to /mfa-verify even after a successful push approval; incognito works but normal browser doesn't. they say clearing cookies helps but that's not a viable UX. ?
ryan_engineer: can you drop the exact repro steps and any request/response traces they have?
jules_support: repro steps from acme IT: 1) admin forces password reset for a user 2) user logs in with new password 3) gets prompted for MFA push 4) user approves on device 5) browser redirects to /mfa-verify again (loop). They captured a couple of network snippets and a trace-id: trace=tr-9a7b2c. They pasted the response header that sets a session cookie: 

Set-Cookie: session_id=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=.acme.com; Max-Age=3600; Secure; HttpOnly

but their frontend sees two session cookies (session_id and session_id_old) for .acme.com.
sara_security: interesting — two cookies same name? or different names? looks like stale cookie leftover from previous session. could be cookie domain/path overlap or our session rotation not expiring the old cookie. request/response logs?
jules_support: acme says server responded with Set-Cookie for session_id but the browser kept sending session_id_old which the app treats as authenticated but with mismatched device_trust flag. they also see a 401 from /api/v1/auth/status occasionally. they sent this snippet: 

Request (user approve): POST /auth/mfa/verify 200
Response headers: 
Set-Cookie: session_id=eyJnew...; Path=/; Domain=.acme.com; Secure; HttpOnly
Cache-Control: max-age=0, no-cache

But after redirect the client requested /mfa-verify and got 302 to /login which then redirected back to /mfa-verify.
ryan_engineer: OK can reproduce locally using a cookie pair scenario. quick hypothesis: when we rotate session after password reset we set a new cookie but we don't explicitly clear the previous cookie name variant that older clients may be sending. Also if CDN or ingress strips Vary:Cookie or caches Set-Cookie, browser could keep using old cookie. infra team — any CDN rules that might cache Set-Cookie responses for /auth/*? @ops_oncall @infra-bot
ops_oncall: infra-bot shows no CDN cache rules for auth endpoints. edge cache is bypassed for cookies by default in our config. tagging logs for trace tr-9a7b2c to the auth-service pod.
infra-bot: deploying log-sampler to auth-service (selector=app=auth, env=prod) to capture trace=tr-9a7b2c. ETA ~3m.
ryan_engineer: in the meantime, two quick things for support to try with customer: 1) confirm if cookie names differ (session_id vs session_id_old) and ask them to export document.cookie to confirm duplicates; 2) ask them to inspect cookie SameSite attribute and subdomain usage. if they have multiple subdomains (app.acme.com vs acme.com) cookie domain mismatch can cause two cookies to coexist.
jules_support: asked them to paste document.cookie and they sent: 

"session_id=eyJold...; session_id_old=eyJstale...; other=..."

they said session_id_old predates the password reset by weeks. frontend code prefers session_id (new) but server-side session lookup finds session_id_old in fallback and thinks device_trust=false which triggers additional verification. that mismatch creates a loop.
sara_security: that matches a design gap — we should ensure session rotation invalidates previous cookies via Set-Cookie with Max-Age=0 for the old cookie name and correct Domain/Path to clear on browser. Do we currently emit a cookie-clear header?
ryan_engineer: not for the legacy cookie name. new auth flow writes `session_id` but legacy flow used `session_id_old`. we kept backward-compat for transitional clients. after password reset we expected clients to drop the old cookie, but clearly some don't.
ops_oncall: I pulled the auth-service logs for tr-9a7b2c — multiple sessions referenced: 

[auth-service] trace=tr-9a7b2c user=alice user_id=usr_123 checking session: session_id_old found in request, lookup returned stale_session (device_trust=false) => triggers mfa enforcement => response sets new session_id but does not set cookie-clear for session_id_old.

ryan_engineer: OK root cause likely: leftover legacy cookie name causing server to treat request as stale. fix options: - immediately push a small auth release that always emits a Set-Cookie clearing `session_id_old` on any session create/rotate - update server to ignore `session_id_old` if a `session_id` is present in request (but that may be brittle) - provide customer-side workaround to delete cookie via JS or admin-initiated global logout.
jules_support: customer asked for quick workaround they can deploy — they want something server-side if possible. they don't want every user to have to clear cookies manually.
sara_security: agree push a server-side clear. Ryan can we ship a hotfix that on successful auth we add: 

Set-Cookie: session_id_old=; Path=/; Domain=.acme.com; Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly

and ensure domain/path match what the old cookie used. also add SameSite attribute match.
ryan_engineer: yes, that's straightforward. will open a tiny PR to auth repo to set cookie clear on rotate. will also add a one-off migration step to publish a Set-Cookie for both names for 24h to coax browsers to overwrite the old value with empty. target deploy in next 1 hour.
ops_oncall: rolling canary in progress. auth-service v2.13.4-hotfix -> canary pod passed health checks.
infra-bot: canary traffic: 5% -> success.
ryan_engineer: canary looks good. deploying to 100% now.
infra-bot: deploy completed. all auth-service instances updated.
ops_oncall: I confirmed through logs for trace tr-9a7b2c — subsequent requests show Set-Cookie clearing session_id_old and the client then uses session_id only. acme IT also confirmed that affected user can now complete MFA and no longer loops.
jules_support: relaying to customer and closing the high-severity ticket after they verify for 24h. asking if we should notify other customers about potential stale legacy cookie problems?
sara_security: send a short post to #announcements and note that any customers using older clients or custom domains might have leftover cookie variants. recommend customers roll out clearing header as needed. we'll also include a KB article explaining how to force logout users from the admin console and how to validate cookies in browser.
ryan_engineer: follow-ups for engineering: 1) create a small unit/integration test to ensure legacy cookie clearing happens on rotate 2) audit other endpoints that set cookies for inconsistent names/domains 3) add an entry in runbook for cookie rollover 4) consider automatic cookie-name migration tool. I'll file GH issues.
ops_oncall: marking incident resolved, severity lowered. will keep ticket open for monitoring 24h.
jules_support: thanks team. closing thread once acme confirms. :white_check_mark:
